nodes.label: Lab client profile
nodes.rationale: final: true closes the tests those readings cover, but closing the order is a separate transition because a lab may still have more to add to a specimen whose first test is done. A correction is simply a new reading on a still-completed test.

nodes.label: Corrections via replaced_by_uuid
nodes.rationale: A corrected result never overwrites the previous one: it creates a new row and marks the old with replaced_by_uuid, because the national node may already have distributed the wrong value. The national node receives both and knows which counts.

nodes.label: Tracking number format
nodes.rationale: MZ-<facility_code>-<yyddd>-<seq>, always generated by the local node, with uniqueness enforced by a unique index rather than by reading the last row — the current TrackingNumberTrail.last approach collides under concurrency. The number never changes even when the specimen crosses two institutions.

nodes.label: Transactional core schema
nodes.rationale: patients, orders, order_tests, test_results, an append-only status_events replacing the several *_trails, referrals, and sync_outbox replacing the four *_sync_trackers with their slightly different semantics.

nodes.label: Native statuses in FHIR extensions
nodes.rationale: FHIR's status vocabulary is narrower than the system's — a lab-rejected specimen and a facility-cancelled order both map to revoked — so the native status is published in order-status, test-status, test-panel, revision and replaced-by extensions.

nodes.label: SISLAB_SYNC_LAB_CODE
nodes.rationale: The single identity a node must receive: facility, name and district are read from the replicated national labs registry entry, and issued API keys inherit them. Until the registry arrives the code itself prefixes tracking numbers. The older SISLAB_SYNC_NODE_CODE is still read and means the same for nodes installed before the registry existed.

nodes.label: Favicon and Apple Touch Icon Slot
nodes.norm_label: favicon and apple touch icon slot

nodes.label: Flat Geometry Scales Without Detail Loss
nodes.norm_label: flat geometry scales without detail loss

nodes.label: One Raster Asset Serves Every Icon Role
nodes.norm_label: one raster asset serves every icon role

nodes.label: external_mappings table
nodes.rationale: Each EMR and SISLAB installation has inherited codes; instead of stuffing them into the dictionary they live in their own table keyed by system and client, replacing the old name_mappings which could only map text to text.

nodes.label: dictionary:seed initial catalogue load
nodes.rationale: db/dictionary/mlab_catalog.json ships with the release; seeding is idempotent because identity comes from the mLab id through ExternalMapping. After this initial load the catalogue is owned by the national node and new tests are created by hand in the UI.

nodes.label: National dictionary and its synchronisation
nodes.rationale: Write authority over the catalogue is restricted to the national node; local nodes hold a read-only replica pulled by cursor.

nodes.label: mLab import (database and API paths)
nodes.rationale: Both paths share one importer, one ExternalMapping identity and the same idempotency, differing only in row source. The API path is for when only mLab HTTP is reachable, and carries three limits it reports at the end: paediatric/oncological tests and panels are omitted by API listings (and are withdrawn if a prior DB import created them), indicators arrive only through a test that uses them, and a test whose department is retired returns 404 on detail so it imports without indicators or organisms.

nodes.label: each_page cursor paging
nodes.rationale: Saving the cursor after every page (not at the end) is what lets the process die between pages and resume without losing or repeating a reading. The cursor is a locked-counter revision, never a date, so nothing can be written slowly enough to fall behind a cursor that already passed it. Each reading carries its own context so archiving needs no second call.

nodes.label: Client-side Idempotency-Key
nodes.rationale: Networks between a clinic and its lab drop mid-request; without the key a retry is a second specimen nobody collected. Passing your own key means even a retry from another process is recognised.

nodes.label: Clinical term resolution policy
nodes.rationale: Terms may be given by national_code, uuid or name (a bare string counts as { name }). An unrecognised term is not refused: the national catalogue is still being consolidated, and refusing the test a lab runs every day because the list has not reached it obstructs work instead of protecting it. Only a term naming nothing is refused.

nodes.label: Cursor pagination (since / next_cursor / has_more)
nodes.rationale: since is the numeric revision of a change, not a time; the client feeds meta.next_cursor back as since until meta.has_more is false.

nodes.label: Duplicate /api/v3/results path entry
nodes.rationale: The path key /api/v3/results appears twice; the first entry duplicates showOrderResults' body under the listResults operationId with a truncated, spliced description, and YAML last-key-wins silently discards it. Looks like a bad merge rather than intent.

nodes.label: fhirCapabilityStatement operation
nodes.rationale: The only FHIR route present in this document, so the facade is discoverable from it while its real contract is the generated CapabilityStatement — which, being built from the constants the controllers use, cannot diverge from what the node serves.

nodes.label: HL7 FHIR R4 facade
nodes.rationale: Every resource is projected from the transactional models and admission re-enters the same OrderRequest component as the native API, so dictionary validation and panel expansion cannot diverge. Auth, scopes, facility scoping, rate limiting, idempotency and audit are properties of the node, not of the dialect; only response shape differs.

nodes.label: FHIR results feed by revision cursor
nodes.norm_label: fhir results feed by revision cursor
nodes.rationale: _since is a sequential revision from a locked counter, not a timestamp, so a reading whose transaction is slow to commit cannot land behind a cursor that already moved past it. Corrections never rewrite the earlier reading: the replaced one moves again in the feed as entered-in-error with a replaced-by extension, and $acknowledge on it is refused with 409 naming the replacement.

nodes.label: OpenAPI spec served with Scalar
nodes.rationale: Each node serves /api-docs.json filtered to the endpoints its own mode actually exposes, and CI cross-checks the spec against live routes, domain enums and every response the suite produces, in both directions.

nodes.label: Dual coding: national code plus LOINC
nodes.norm_label: dual coding: national code plus loinc
nodes.rationale: Every CodeableConcept always carries the national code first and LOINC only where curation has mapped it, so LOINC coverage can grow without any client change.

nodes.label: SISLAB Sync OpenAPI 3.1 contract
nodes.rationale: The formal reference, validated continuously in CI against application routes and against the responses the suite produces (spec/contracts/openapi_spec.rb).

nodes.label: Tolerance of unknown clinical terms
nodes.rationale: The catalogue is a reference, not a barrier. A term the node does not recognise is stored exactly as it arrived and linked later when the catalogue reaches it, without re-entering the reading; the national node no longer blocks a node's queue over a code it lacks. The only remaining refusal is a term that names nothing at all, because then nobody would know what was requested or measured.

nodes.label: Database default connection (env-driven)
nodes.rationale: Every setting comes from the environment so the same image can be a local node or the national one with nothing but a different .env file.

nodes.label: app service (Puma)
nodes.rationale: Only the code is mounted; gems stay in the image. A named volume for gems would keep whatever was installed the first time, so adding a gem to the Gemfile would fail at boot while the rebuild looked successful.

nodes.label: css service (Tailwind watcher)
nodes.rationale: Tailwind compiles into app/assets/builds on the mounted volume, so the watcher is its own service rather than something the web process must remember to start. In production the build happens once, in the image.

nodes.label: Swappable Transport
nodes.rationale: The node drives this client against itself in its own tests without opening a socket; any object answering call(method:, path:, params:, body:, headers:) with [status, headers, body] serves.

nodes.label: READ-COMMITTED transaction isolation
nodes.rationale: The replication cursor is ordered by a row lock held until commit, which works at any isolation level, so repeatable reads buy nothing and cost portability: MariaDB 11.6+ enables innodb_snapshot_isolation by default and a locking read of a row that moved since the snapshot then fails outright instead of reading the current version as MySQL does. Under READ COMMITTED both engines behave alike, and a reader polling for changes wants the latest committed rows anyway.

nodes.label: TEST_DATABASE_NAME separation
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not DATABASE_NAME: a node's .env points that at the database the node actually runs on and every environment reads the same file, so a test run honouring it truncates the working database and db:seed writes demo data into the one the suite is about to assert against. Both have happened.

nodes.label: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME side-by-side nodes
nodes.rationale: Which node the stack is comes entirely from .env; running a local and a national node side by side (needed from S9 onwards) is done by giving each its own directory and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME.

nodes.label: Dual operating modes (local / national)
nodes.rationale: One artefact, one image, two mutually exclusive roles: the local node bridges the EMR and SISLAB and queues outbox events; the national node owns the master-data catalogue and orchestrates referrals. Routes, jobs and tasks load conditionally so the same build serves both.

nodes.label: SISLAB_SYNC_MODE
nodes.rationale: Mode is parameterised only by this env var and boot aborts if it is unset, so the mode can never be implicit or half-configured.

nodes.label: Dual-mode CI matrix
nodes.rationale: Both local and national modes are exercised on every push so that a route or an initializer that only works in one of them fails in CI rather than at a deployed site. fail-fast is off so one mode's failure does not hide the other's.

nodes.label: Node client profile
nodes.rationale: Delivery is at-least-once and storage is idempotent by event_uuid, so the same batch arriving twice is recognised rather than duplicated; application is in sequence per aggregate, an event whose predecessor is missing waits, and the response names in `rejected` what the capital could not apply. Batches cap at 500.

nodes.label: At-least-once delivery with idempotency
nodes.rationale: The national node accepts each event_uuid exactly once, so resending is safe by construction rather than by coordination.

nodes.label: Per-aggregate ordering by sequence
nodes.rationale: sequence is scoped to aggregate_uuid; an out-of-order event waits for its predecessor instead of being applied wrongly.

nodes.label: Sample referral round trip
nodes.rationale: Three codes travel with the specimen — sending_facility_code, receiving_lab_code and lab_code (the section) — and the tracking number never changes across institutions. The gap between dispatched_at and received_at is the transport metric nobody can measure today.

nodes.label: sync_outbox
nodes.rationale: The event is written in the same transaction that changes the domain. Nothing is deleted: delivered_at is stamped, failures keep last_error and count attempts with exponential backoff and manual reprocessing from the UI, and a rejected event returns with a code and stays visible in the sync queue instead of vanishing into logs.

nodes.label: x-node-mode operation availability
nodes.rationale: Each node exposes only the endpoints of its mode, so every operation declares local, national or both and the served /api-docs.json can be filtered from one global document.

nodes.label: draft → active promotion gate
nodes.rationale: Because distribution is a continuous delta rather than published versions, quality control moves into the record's state: an edit starts as draft, only enters the delta when promoted to active, and the promotion is audited with author and date. Otherwise one bad edit reaches every laboratory in minutes.

nodes.label: Fixed decisions register
nodes.rationale: Decisions taken before the plan, each mapped to the steps that must be revisited if it changes: greenfield on branch v2, Hotwire+Tailwind in-app, local pushes and pulls while national never initiates, dictionary loaded from mLab then owned nationally, hashed scoped API keys, uuid plus readable national code, delta by cursor with no published versions, everything replicated including patient NID, and one Docker artefact for both modes.

nodes.label: Monotonic revision cursor
nodes.rationale: The cursor cannot be updated_at: two concurrent transactions can write updated_at in a different order from the one in which they become visible, so the local node advances past the slower change and loses it permanently. The revision is a global sequence assigned at commit, and S3's concurrency test exists to prove there are no gaps.

nodes.label: Risk register and mitigations
nodes.rationale: Chief risks: an unversioned delta spreading a bad edit within minutes, a time-based cursor losing changes permanently, mLab catalogue quality, intermittent local networks, identifiable patient data at the national node, dependence on the SISLAB/EMR teams, and a single developer — with S11 explicitly reducible to dashboard, order search and key management if S10/S11 slip.

nodes.label: Assumptions and out of scope
nodes.rationale: Assumes Ruby 3.3+/Rails 8/MySQL 8/Redis/Sidekiq, the Mozambican NID as patient identifier, work on branch v2 with main untouched until the v2.0.0 tag, and TLS terminated by a proxy in front of the application in both modes. No historical data migration, because NLIMS is not in production. Out of scope: changing mLab/SISLAB code, EMR-side adapters, mobile app and label printing.

nodes.label: Migrations at container start
nodes.rationale: bin/docker-entrypoint runs db:prepare only when the container command includes 'rails server', so the app container migrates while the Sidekiq and ephemeral containers do not — avoiding concurrent migration runs.

nodes.label: SISLAB_SYNC_TLS_TERMINATED
nodes.rationale: assume_ssl marks every request secure before force_ssl's redirect is evaluated, so a node served over plain HTTP with the default redirects nothing and merely claims a scheme it does not practise: the session cookie is Secure and never returned (web login does not persist), request.base_url resolves to https://host:3000 so FHIR Bundle fullUrl/link point at a non-TLS port and a following client makes Puma log Invalid HTTP format, and HSTS over plain HTTP is ignored by conforming browsers (RFC 6797 §8.1). Setting it false disables no protection the transport has; it aligns config with the transport actually in use.

nodes.label: SISLAB Sync v2 rebuild plan
nodes.rationale: Twelve weeks, one developer, no backward compatibility: a single artefact running in two modes that becomes the SISLAB dictionary, the EMR entry point and the inter-facility referral network at once.

nodes.label: Production deployment
nodes.rationale: Production uses the final Dockerfile image (non-privileged user, precompiled assets, no host mount), distinct from the development stage Compose consumes. The same image serves both node kinds; mode is read from the environment at runtime and never baked in.

nodes.label: The national node never initiates a connection
nodes.norm_label: the national node never initiates a connection
nodes.rationale: Local nodes sit behind NAT with no fixed address, so every connection starts on the local side. The dictionary cascades national → local → SISLAB over the same delta contract, letting a local node serve it while disconnected, and no laboratory operation blocks when the national node is unreachable.

nodes.label: The twelve steps S1–S12
nodes.rationale: One week per step, sequential; a step closes only when its 'done when' criterion is verifiable by another person, and each ends with something demonstrable plus named commits.

nodes.label: sislab_sync_client reference gem
nodes.rationale: Exists to give the three integrations one envelope, one way to page a cursor, one exception per refusal the node can give, and the idempotency that makes a retry safe on a line that drops.

nodes.label: Relaxed RSpec cops
nodes.rationale: ExampleLength and MultipleExpectations are disabled because long descriptive example names read better in a spec list; SpecFilePathFormat is disabled because spec/sislab_sync_spec.rb describes the SislabSync module, not a class file under app/.

nodes.label: me as the first diagnostic call
nodes.norm_label: me as the first diagnostic call
nodes.rationale: It separates a wrong key from a wrong scope from a wrong node, which otherwise all look like 'it doesn't work'.

nodes.label: Zero runtime dependencies by design
nodes.rationale: A laboratory server with no route to rubygems can still install it, or simply copy lib/.

nodes.label: Session and authorisation messages (pt)
nodes.rationale: The sign-in screen states that accounts are created by the node administrator and that API keys are a different thing that cannot be used to log in — separating user sessions from API credentials at the point of confusion.

nodes.label: API key carries node identity
nodes.rationale: A local node is a laboratory: the key inherits the node's own lab and facility codes and codes declared in a request body are ignored in their favour. Only a node-to-node client speaking for another node is refused, with 403 lab_mismatch.

nodes.label: API key format ssk_<env>_<prefix>_<secret>
nodes.rationale: Replaces the token+appuuid pair with short expiry. The secret is stored as SHA-256 and compared in constant time; the public prefix is indexed for O(1) lookup instead of scanning every key. The key carries facility_code and lab_code, so acting on another facility gets 403 even with a valid key.

nodes.label: API key scopes
nodes.rationale: A local node is a laboratory and knows which: a key inherits the lab code and the facility from the registry entry, so codes declared in a request body are ignored rather than refused.

nodes.label: National laboratory registry (labs)
nodes.rationale: labs is a dictionary entity like any other, published on the same revision/cursor channel, so referrals need only to_lab_code and nobody writes facility codes by hand. An unknown code is refused because a parcel addressed to a typo never arrives; a node that has not yet received the registry still works, using its own code as prefix and accepting any destination.

nodes.label: Portuguese locale (default UI language)
nodes.rationale: Portuguese is the default and no view carries fixed text; the locale file carries the whole operator vocabulary — navigation, dashboard sync stats, outbox counters and cursors.

nodes.label: One exception class per refusal
nodes.rationale: Always branch on the class or the code: the message is Portuguese, written for a person, and may be rewritten at any time.

nodes.label: Automatic RateLimited retry
nodes.rationale: Waits what Retry-After says, up to three times. A transport error is retried only where retrying cannot do the work twice — a read, or a write carrying an Idempotency-Key.

nodes.label: ErrorCode enum
nodes.rationale: The stable programmatic code lives in `code` and the human description in `message`, so clients branch on the code and messages stay free to be rewritten.
